page: Google Cloud Platform n1-highcpu-8 is a compute-skewed virtual machine instance configured with 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores and 7.0 GB of system memory. Powered by an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.3 GHz with 45 MB of L3 cache, the system features dedicated hyper-threaded compute resources. It includes hardware acceleration instruction sets such as AVX, AES, BMI2, and FMA, but lacks newer vector extensions like AVX-512 or AMX. The instance includes no local storage or bundled GPUs, requiring external network block storage for persistent data operations.

Benchmark outcomes show modest per-core and parallel computational throughput on modern workloads. The instance achieved 914.0 on Geekbench single-core and 3,557.0 on multi-core testing, falling into lower benchmark percentiles due to its legacy CPU generation. Similarly, stress-ng recorded 1,109.79 for single-core and 5,820.12 for multi-core performance. Memory throughput remains steady on large blocks, reaching 47.28 GB/sec for uncached reads and 34.7 GB/sec for writes. PassMark overall CPU scoring placed in the middle tier at 6,786.78, with a ray tracing score of 6,021.0 on Geekbench.

Cost efficiency for this instance is shaped by its high vCPU-to-memory ratio, providing roughly 0.9 GB of RAM per vCPU. While the older architecture delivers lower raw throughput per core compared to newer cloud platforms, it offers a budget-conscious entry point for multi-threaded tasks that do not demand extensive memory. Tradeoffs include poor single-threaded decompression metrics, low database operation scores (2,431.16 on PassMark), and the absence of bundled local storage.

The hardware configuration suits horizontal batch processing, lightweight build farms, multi-threaded CPU-bound microservices, and general compute tasks that require low memory overhead per processing thread.

Driven by a 2.3 GHz Intel Xeon x86_64 processor with 45 MB L3 cache, the system includes support for AVX, AES, and FMA instructions without AVX-512 capabilities. It provides no local disk storage or hardware GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached storage. With limited memory per core, this instance is suited for multi-threaded compute workloads with low memory footprints, including code compilation, distributed compute workers, and batch processing pipelines.
